sermon.title: Messianic Prophecies
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Messianic Prophecies,” Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Isaiah 7, 8 and 9, showing how Isaiah breaks into prophecy about natural Israel with prophecies of Jesus: the virgin and Emmanuel, the children for signs and wonders, Galilee of the nations, and the names of Jesus in Isaiah 9:6-7. He then applies the Prince of Peace and the kingdom’s increase to the church’s lack of unity and righteousness.

Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the captions spell Naphtali several different ways (Neptula, Napali, Nepali, Nebuli) and Capernaum as “Capernium”; these are corrected to the Bible spellings because he is reading Isaiah 9:1 and Matthew 4:13. He also discusses sexual abuse of children in the church and makes remarks about homosexuals. These are his own words and are kept as spoken. He says God is interested in the nations, that Jesus is the light to those in the shadow of death, and that what Jesus preached was repentance.

He says the government is on his shoulders, so it is his responsibility to reveal the kingdom to us, and that Jesus is the eternal God and cannot be separated from his word.

Isaiah 9:6 and 7. “For to us a child is born, a son is given.” Okay? If you want to learn about Jesus, you go to the Old Testament and learn about him as well as the New Testament. You get it? Why do we need the New Testament? Because the truth of God’s word is in the Old Testament. And you want to learn about Jesus, you got to not only read the New Testament, you got to read the Old. And here we find what his names are. And his names always describe him. Okay. “A son is given. The government,” the empire, the dominion, the kingdom which he preached. The kingdom of God is here at hand. Okay. “The kingdom of God is upon his shoulders.” It’s his responsibility to get me and turn me to the kingdom of God.

It’s his responsibility. It’s not my responsibility. My responsibility is to seek him. My responsibility is to read the word. My responsibility is to pray and worship him. Then it’s his responsibility to reveal the kingdom to me. The kingdom is where? Within us. See, Christ in us, the hope of glory. Christ be formed in us. So the responsibility is on his shoulders. And that’s a big relief to me. You see, all my grunting and groaning and prayer and all that isn’t going to do anything when I just talk to him in prayer and I worship him and I read the Bible, he comes and he does. He carries the load. Isn’t that good? Yeah. And he’s faithful. Even when I mess up, he still is responsible.

Come on, Dave. Get up. We got to get the kingdom in you, boy. Amen. Yeah, that’s what he does. “His name, okay, shall be called Wonderful,” extraordinary. See, he does what ordinary people cannot do. Respond to him, and then he is extraordinary, and he works in you in extraordinary ways. Hallelujah. “He is the Counselor,” the adviser.

Is he the adviser? Yeah. Yeah. And his word is our adviser all the days of our pilgrimage. It’s important that you understand you cannot separate Jesus and his word. If you say you love Jesus, you’re going to be reading the Bible. Why? Because he is the living word. And he is going to drive you to read that book. And through these things, he works himself in you. Hallelujah. Because it’s his job. Okay. Now, his name is “Almighty God.” Oh, here he is. God. They’re calling him God again. He’s the mighty God. He’s the, the mighty is there.

It’s the strong champion, the chief champion. Is Christ the champion of the church? Is he God by this title? Yes, he’s God. We’re only preachers. [unclear] has no great ability to convert anybody. Neither does Oprah Winfrey, nor [unclear], nor Billy Graham. That’s the bottom line. But he does that in the measure of the word. See, we got to have the word preached. And the word isn’t being preached in America like it is right now in South America, Africa, and Asia, where tremendous revival is going on and millions are getting saved every year. Just millions are coming to Christ with supernatural signs and wonders. And I’m praying God just kind of turn that wind around and blow up on North America again. How many would say amen to that? Yeah. And these people are getting filled with the Holy Ghost. They’re speaking in tongues and signs and wonders are happening. People are getting delivered. It’s, it’s just amazing. But in America, I, we need the wind turned to us. Don’t leave us out, boy. “And he’s the Prince of Peace.”

chunks.section_question: What does he say about imitators, false prophets and apostles?
chunks.short_answer: He says God raised up teachers and prophets in a visitation, that imitators then came in, and he uses the sons who tried to cast out a demon as an example. He says a prophet whose predictions do not come to pass is false, and that a true apostle is an ambassador who has signs and wonders and is patient with God’s people.
chunks.text:
I mean, you go back there, it’s pretty babyish. But after the [unclear] 40 visitation of God, God raised up teachers who could shoot the word with an arrow and hit the target instead of a scatter gun hoping that somewhere it hit people. The revelation of God’s word started coming out, and you had some prominent teachers of the, you also had some prophets that could nail it at the beginning of this stuff. And I’ve been teaching at the home Bible study. At the beginning of this visitation, it was a pure stream. You know, there were no imitators. This thing was real. And these prophets nailed it every time. And then the imitators come in. Ah, God.

These people that see something, like the sons of [unclear], you know, they saw Paul casting out demons, and they, boy, they got a demon-possessed guy and they’re wanting to cast him out, and the demon says, “Man, Paul I know and Jesus I know, but who in the world are you guys?” And he beat him up, took their clothes off, and they ran out of the house naked. Why? They were imitators of what God was doing real in another person. And folks, we got to realize, we got to accept our gifts. We got to accept our abilities and be happy with them, even if they’re none, because it hurts when we pretend something is happening that is not happening. And right now we are a joke to the world. We have all these varieties of churches and we fight and quarrel with one another.

We cannot stand in unity for anything in America. And the world just laughs at us. He said, “I’ll send you teachers, prophets,” and he also said, I will, said, I will send you apostles and wise men. All in the same statement. Now, folks, as I showed you, I’ve seen the teachers. I was there when people were teaching that couldn’t teach beans. And I was there when that teacher came along that, oh my God, it just opened up the word to you. It just changed your life. I was there when the prophets were nailing it. They were speaking things that nobody would know but the Holy Ghost. And they were nailing it. And it was changing lives.

But they’re not around anymore. These Kansas City prophets have been pro... prophets. I don’t know if you’ve heard of the Kansas City prophets, but they’ve been false prophets since, ever since they started. And people are still following them. And they claim to be tongue talkers and all the rest. But folks, when you make predictions and they don’t come to pass, the Bible says you’re a false prophet. I don’t care if you’re a nice guy. I don’t care if you speak in tongues. I don’t care what. You need to shut your mouth. Could that be an amen? We need the real thing. But folks, I’ve never seen wisdom restored back yet. If you have, show it to me. I haven’t seen it. These denominations don’t have wisdom. And the Catholic Church certainly don’t have wisdom. The Pope just approved homosexual unions. He don’t have the authority to do that.

I don’t care what kind of titles on him. When the Bible says a sin is a sin, it’s a sin. There’s no leader down here can change the Bible. Hallelujah. See, we don’t have wisdom in the church. chunks.section_question: What does Isaiah 9 say about leaders who flatter or seduce people into sin?
chunks.short_answer: He reads Isaiah 9:13-16 and says God will cut off the head and the tail, the elders and the prophet who teaches lies, who flatter people to stay as they are or seduce them. He says the end is destruction, hurt and pain, but like Isaiah, in God’s presence we see our sin and receive power to change.
chunks.text:
He gives a word to natural and spiritual Israel. Very powerful. He’s going to repeat something he said in Isaiah 3. Isaiah 9:13-16. “The people turn not to him that smites them, neither do they seek the Lord of hosts.” See, it’s not just Ahaz that’s evil. The people are following Ahaz. They’re bad. And the Lord has smoked them. He’s come and corrected them, and they don’t take correction. “For this reason, the Lord will cut off from Israel the head and the tail, the branch and the reed in one day.” The elder and the honorable, he’s the head. And the prophet that teaches lies, he’s the tail.

And God said, “I’m going to deal with these leaders that are flattering my people to sin or leading my people into sin, seducing them.” It could be either way. They can flatter us and tell us we’re okay, or they can seduce us and make us feel intimidated because we want to do right and they’re saying it’s okay to do wrong. So, I’m going to cut them off. Do we need that kind of leadership cut off in America? Yes. “For the leaders of these people cause them to err,” the elders, the honorable and the false prophets, they’re causing the people to err, as he said in 3:12, “and they that are led of them are destroyed.” So whether they’re seducing us or flattering us to stay the way we are, the end is what?

Destruction in our life. Hurt and pain in our life. Hallelujah. But like Isaiah, when the glory of God came, then Isaiah said, “Oh, I see my sin. And he can say, Lord, you got me there. I don’t always speak like I should, but see, in the presence of God, in the glory of God, he saw his area is error and the empowerment to change it. And that’s what we need.
